title: Register changes after the E01 static run, V2-S2-003-PR2
description: What V2-S2-003-PR2 changed in the register once the static parts of V2-E01 had run under their merged freeze record: every register change with its value before and after, and the findings each answers. It is the third ledger written after v1.0.0 was released, and like the two before it, it is not part of the pack that release was cut over: the evidence index undoes it, with the other post-release ledgers, to recompute that pack. It adds one claim, certified at C0 on the one record it adds with it, and moves no existing claim's status or record. It raises and closes no blocker, declares no freeze, states no release, and edits no dated record.

claim.statement: Under the frozen E01 procedure, two renders of the V1 synchronous reference contract on its local binding, in two processes, wrote byte-identical release input that records its sources; a replica-range change moved only the values and release fields it owns; and six invalid or conflicting inputs were each refused twice with the registered rule, category, and code, writing nothing.
claim.limitation: Static, C0, from one run on one host: the renderer ran as a tool and its release input was inspected, for one contract on one binding. Nothing was deployed, reconciled, or served. The platform-defaults revision a release records is asserted, not reconstructed, and the two hand-written strings that repeat contract pins are not checked against the contract.
claim.doesNotEstablish: That the release input deploys or serves, which E01-D owns and has not run; determinism for another workload shape, contract, or binding; reliability under failure; or production readiness.

evidenceRecords.summary: On 2026-10-02 the static parts of V2-E01 ran once, as freeze revision 1 registers them, at the merged revision 707e29f4a0ff31ea90fa33f6b8cf2ec883cfb6a3 with every pinned input unchanged and nothing uncommitted before the run; E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C each PASSED, and python -m tools.experiment_e01 --check judges the committed run again from its raw evidence.

executedComponents.note: tools/experiment_e01, run from a byte copy outside the checked-out tree, which parsed the pinned inputs and called the render package's generate_release, write_release, and admit_manual_values in process; the run manifest records each runner file's digest.
src/inferops/domain/render at the executing revision, the generator whose release input was inspected, as helm template is for the chart's rendered manifests.
python -m tools.experiment_e01 --check, computing every verdict again from the committed files and comparing it with the recorded outcomes, file digests, and result page.

workload.description: No workload was issued. The inputs were the pinned contract, binding, chart defaults, hand-written values, and V1 values, read as files, with the edits the freeze record registers.

environment.note: One Windows host, version 10.0.26200, Python 3.12.12 under uv 0.9.16 (a63e5b62e 2025-12-06), in a detached worktree at the executing revision with no change before the run and only the run's evidence directory after it, on 2026-10-02; no cluster, network, runtime, or model was contacted.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The two renders are canonically identical: both files are byte-identical, the SHA-256 of each file is equal, and metadata.releaseId is equal.
The release records the source contract digest, and it equals contract_digest of the parsed contract.
The release records the EnvironmentBinding's name, apiVersion, and digest, and they equal local-kind, inferops.io/v1alpha1, and binding_digest of the parsed binding.

The release records the generated values digest, and it equals the SHA-256 of the bytes of the values file beside it. The renderer and platform-defaults revisions it records equal the executing commit.

No claim-relevant workload intent is written by hand after rendering, except the model.artifact.sourceUrl and model.license.reference strings, which repeat contract pins (definition.limitations): admit_manual_values admits the hand-written values with no finding; every chart value that a workload-intent context value renders to is in the generated values file; and the generated and hand-written values, merged over the chart's defaults, equal the V1 real values merged the same way, except telemetry.deploymentEnvironment, which is local in V2 and dev in V1 as the V1 synchronous compatibility record states.

The mutation changes only the expected semantic output: in values.generated.yaml, only runtime.replicaCount, from 1 to 2; in rendered-workload-release.yaml, only metadata.releaseId, output.helmValues.sha256, and source.contract.sha256; and source.contract.sha256 equals contract_digest of the mutated contract.

Every negative case is refused at its registered step with its expected refusal: for a RenderRefused, exactly the registered findings, in order, each with its rule, category, code, and field; for E01-C-4, the registered exception type, code, and field. No case writes an output directory, and each case's second execution gives the same refusal as its first.

results.statement: render-a and render-b, written by two processes with PYTHONHASHSEED 1 and 2, are byte-identical in both files, and both releases carry the same metadata.releaseId.
The render-a release records the source contract digest, and it equals contract_digest of the parsed contract.
The render-a release records the binding as local-kind, inferops.io/v1alpha1, with the digest binding_digest gives for the parsed binding.
The render-a release records the SHA-256 of the values file beside it, and the executing revision as both its renderer and its platform-defaults revision.

admit_manual_values admitted the hand-written values with no finding, all 20 workload-intent chart values are in the generated file, and the two merged value sets differ only at telemetry.deploymentEnvironment, local in V2 and dev in V1.

Setting the replica range to two moved runtime.replicaCount from 1 to 2 and no other value, and moved only metadata.releaseId, output.helmValues.sha256, and source.contract.sha256 in the release, the last equal to contract_digest of the mutated contract.
Each of the six negative cases was refused at its registered step with exactly its registered refusal, wrote no output directory, and was refused the same way when run a second time.

limitations: One run on one Windows host at one revision, with one contract on one binding.
The renderer ran as a tool and its release input was inspected; the release input was not deployed, reconciled, or served.
The platform-defaults revision a release records is asserted, not reconstructed, and the download URL and licence reference that repeat contract pins are not checked against the contract.
The runner is not a pinned input of the freeze record. It ran from a byte copy outside the checked-out tree, and the run records each runner file's content digest instead.
The runner was first exercised in temporary repositories by its own test suite before the run; those executions are not E01 runs and are not result evidence.
doesNotEstablish: That the release input deploys through Git and Argo CD or serves a completion: E01-D owns that and has not run.
That another workload shape, contract, or binding renders deterministically.
Reliability under failure, or production readiness.

The register states what that run showed, at C0, beside the planned deployment claim it does not satisfy, appended so that no existing pointer into the register moves. The claim's status was decided by the maintainer for this change.

findings.observation: E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C ran once under freeze revision 1 and each PASSED. No claim in the register stated what a static render of the reference contract shows, and the one claim about deployment values is planned and can hold no record: no supported deployment path consumes the generated files, so the run does not show it.
findings.resolution: A new claim states the run's result at C0 and holds its record. The planned deployment claim is unchanged; E01-D, which deploys and serves, is the run that could show it.

findings.observation: The register's reason for the evidence index, a surface that claims nothing, named six ledgers of register changes. This ledger is a seventh, and the released pack is recomputed by undoing it too.
findings.resolution: The reason is replaced; the surface claims nothing.
